title: AI-Driven Adaptive Scanning Provides Accelerated, Efficient and Contextual Data Acquisition for Volume Electron Microscopy of Plant Cells using Plasma FIB-SEM
content: Focused Ion Beam Scanning Electron Microscopy (FIB-SEM), a form of volume Electron Microscopy (vEM), is one of the most versatile platforms for capturing 3D datasets of organelles, cells, and tissues at isotropic and nanoscale resolutions. However, this precise high-resolution approach typically results in the acquisition of many more images and longer cutting/milling times compared to other vEM techniques for similar volumes. While extremely powerful for many important biological questions, including research as well as detection and diagnosis of diseases, this can translate into increased acquisition times (up to many days), increased cost/sample, reduced throughput, and low statistical power (only one or two datasets/condition) [1]. In addition, many samples such as plants, have air spaces, vacuoles, and/or other off target structures that represent a substantial proportion of the tissue but lacks meaningful information for a given study. Enhanced sample staining and/or fast scanning combined with post-acquisition image processing routines to improve image quality are just a few ways to improve sample throughput [2]. Here we describe a new acquisition workflow that leverages an artificial intelligence (AI) driven “Adaptive Scanning” strategy to greatly accelerate the speed and/or volumes acquired via FIB-SEM.
